summary: Two small neural networks train live, side by side, on a 2D toy dataset: a baseline, and one with a single change (dropout, weight decay, residual connections, more depth, or ReLU instead of tanh). The visitor sees both decision boundaries plus train and test loss.
use_for: network architectures, regularization, overfitting, generalization, skip connections, depth, activations, normalization, image classification, supervised learning

technique.help: the single change the second network gets; pick the one closest to the paper's idea

one_liner: Train two tiny networks live, one with the paper's twist, and compare their decision boundaries.
mechanism: The demo trains two small networks on the same 2D points at the same time. They are identical except for one change, so any difference in the boundaries they learn, or in how their training and test losses move, comes from that change alone.
try: Watch the two decision boundaries form, and compare train loss (solid) with test loss (dashed). When train loss keeps falling but test loss rises, the network is memorising noise.
Switch the dataset to Spiral, the hardest one, and see which network untangles it first.
Drag label noise up. Noisy labels are where overfitting shows, and where regularisers earn their keep.
Press New random init a few times. A difference that holds across several initialisations is real, not luck.
simplifications: Both networks are tiny multilayer perceptrons on 2D points, trained with full-batch Adam in your browser. The paper's experiments use real datasets and far larger models.
The networks differ in exactly one feature so the comparison is fair. Real systems combine many such choices, and their effects interact.
